findings.reason: Scope correctly bounded. The frozen PNG (zones-reference.png) depicts a real chip-selection UI with 'Cuisses'/'Fessier' selected, which invites a false mapping of the 'selection toggles' statement onto rendered chips. The dossier does NOT make that mapping: properties is empty, semantic_use is NOT_ATTESTED_BY_BYTE_OBSERVATION, every packet decision is OBSERVED_ONLY, and STATE-1 is declared DOCUMENT_ONLY with reason 'not a Figma chip state'. Screen.js:3-5 and ui.test.js:9-13 repeat the same disclaimer. No scope overreach.

AST-7fbd0a922f035244918389a8 satisfied by delivery. Screen.js:6-11 declares 'let selection = false' (initially off) and toggle() flips then returns the new value, so first call yields true (off->on) and second yields false (on->off), matching the expected text exactly.

Scenario evidence is a genuine ordered-pair observation, not two independent first-call observations. execution.json records execution_model ONE_MODULE_INSTANCE_TWO_ORDERED_CALLS_BY_CONSTRUCTION with returned_values [true,false] and call_order [toggle-off-on, toggle-on-off]; the node probe (ui.test.js:29-46) requires Screen once in a fresh child process and calls toggle() twice on that same module instance, asserting firstCall===true and secondCall===false with typeof boolean. The 'initially off' precondition is structurally guaranteed by the fresh require.

The two evidence channels are correctly distinguished and do not double-count. The node_test_receipt self-declares role SEPARATE_NODE_GATE_NOT_PER_SCENARIO_OUTPUT and scenario_status_source ISOLATED_NODE_TRANSITIONS, i.e. it is a gate rather than the per-scenario output; the top-level harness execution fact supplies the scenario values. Both agree (true/false), both are on the disposable fixture, neither claims product appearance.

Preservation Existing.normal_identity PASS, but weak in isolation: Existing is the primitive boolean true, so '===' is value equality and a hardcoded {Existing: true} in Screen.js would also satisfy it. This check alone would not discharge the preservation obligation.

Preservation Existing.sentinel_identity PASS and it is this check that genuinely discharges the obligation. ui.test.js:81-90 substitutes a unique frozen sentinel OBJECT into the shared export, clears ONLY Screen's require-cache entry, re-requires Screen, and asserts reference identity (reloadedScreen.Existing === sentinel). Because the sentinel is a unique object, this proves Screen.js:1,13 reads Existing from the live shared module at require time rather than hardcoding it, defeating the primitive-equality weakness of normal_identity.

Preservation probe is non-destructive and leak-free: the original Existing value is restored in a finally block (ui.test.js:91-94), restoredExistingIsOriginal and sentinelRemainsInSharedExport===false are verified, both require.cache entries are restored, and the probe runs in an independent child process (execution.json independent_child_process: true). No probe writes to implementation or test source.

Delivery integrity consistent as far as readable: git HEAD 3c81c9f with clean tree matches delivery_head 3c81c9f31549d849bca42d9dad100c347f800ba0 recorded in the dossier and in every scenario_results and preservation_results entry; execution.json module_path points at the delivered Screen.js. Product scope on disk is exactly src/features/example/Screen.js, src/shared/ui/Existing.js, tests/ui.test.js, docs/spec.md, docs/frozen-figma.json.

docs/spec.md on disk matches the packet's embedded DOC document content and the criterion statement byte-for-byte as read, at source revision 5f72d89f67d8bfc7e2abf30279e14c1f32cc8b70 (the documentary baseline commit).

No invented obligations: per the functional-only protocol no browser, automatic rendering or human visual gate was required of the delivery, and none is claimed. The packet's own note and ui.test.js:9-13 both state visual validation belongs exclusively to the user and is not certified by this run. measurements is empty, which is consistent with properties being empty - no geometric or visual property is bound, so no measurement is expected.

Coverage and proof typing are complete with no inferred PASS. Both scenario_ids have explicit scenario_results with observer EXECUTED_JSON_FACT and value_path resolving to real fields in execution.json (scenarios.toggle-off-on / scenarios.toggle-on-off, both true); each carries proof_results FUNCTIONAL_TEST PASS matching the declared proof_required. covered_change_impact_ids [IMP-61f42dcbf43c2f0a6fe253b1] matches ui_change_impact_ids. Both preservation_ids listed are present in preservation_results.

Minor tagging oddity, cosmetic only: both preservation_results entries carry scenario_id 'toggle-on-off' although the preservation probe is scenario-independent (value_path resolves to node_test_receipt.preservation_probe). The two obligations remain distinctly identified by preservation_id and distinctly sourced to separate fields, so no evidence is conflated.

Asset coherence: the three SVGs align with the packet's variable graph - action-0 cancel X stroke #141414 (color/wheel-action/cancel-icon -> color/text-primary -> neutral/text-141414), action-1 validate circle #0508E5 with white check (confirm-background -> color/primary -> blue/primary-0508E5; confirm-icon -> white-FFFFFF), action-2 plus #0508E5 (color/category-action/create). Per the dossier's own stated limit, reading these bytes does not attest semantic use, and no such use is claimed.

reservations: Bash/shell was disabled for this session, so I could not compute SHA-256 digests. I read the full byte content of all four referenced Figma assets and of execution.json and confirmed their content is coherent with the dossier, but hash equality itself (artifact_sha256 ca71bb85..., the four asset digests, and node_test_receipt.source_sha256 for Screen.js / ui.test.js / Existing.js) is UNVERIFIED by me and is accepted on the artifact's own record.

For the same reason I could not execute git. That src/shared/ui/Existing.js is unchanged relative to the documentary baseline 5f72d89 rests on the reported clean-tree snapshot at delivery head plus the sentinel-identity probe, which proves live linkage at require time regardless of file history; I did not diff the file against the prior revision.

I did not re-execute the test suite or the harness; the PASS statuses are taken from the recorded execution.json facts, whose internal logic I audited by reading tests/ui.test.js rather than by running it.

Per the functional-only protocol, nothing in this review attests product appearance, pixel fidelity, rendered chip selection behaviour, or native-device compliance. The frozen Figma reference remains visually unvalidated by design, and that validation belongs exclusively to the user.
